name: QuoteCard
description: One person's words typeset as a quote card, for a scene about what someone said (use it instead of a screenshot of the quote): a speaker plate (round silhouette avatar, bold name, muted role) lands first, a gold quotation badge drops onto the card's top-right corner, then the quote reveals phrase by phrase in a big serif (up to 112 px for a short line, never under 40); hot substrings turn accent with a band sweeping under them, and a small source line closes. The card hugs its content and centres in the box: give it about 760-840 wide x 620-900 tall (it works from 600 x 500 up to wide boxes; a quote at the length limit wants h >= 700).

quote.description: the words, without quotation marks; best at 40-100 Latin characters or 10-40 CJK characters (60 CJK at most). Punctuation splits the reveal into phrases

who.description: the speaker, e.g. Maria Lopez; wraps to two lines when long

role.description: who they are, e.g. owns the noodle shop next door

source.description: small line at the bottom, shown as written, e.g. via Reuters

hot.description: exact substrings of quote to mark in accent after they appear; give one (the accent is the scene's one hot element), two only when they say one thing

at.description: Time the card lands: "line:3" or seconds from the clip start; the quote starts 0.4 s later. Nothing shows before it. Default: the clip start

over.description: seconds the phrase reveal takes (default 0.05 s per Latin or 0.11 s per CJK character, at most 4.5 s; always shortened to leave 1.6 s of the clip for the source and a hold)

color.description: colour of the hot words: theme token or CSS

ground.description: light = cream card with ink text; dark = night card with snow text

example.quote: He gives the bowls away for free, so I sell two hundred fewer a day. I can barely make rent.
example.role: owns the noodle shop next door
